title: Why a planar side cannot create
claim: Why a planar side cannot create, in part. (1) The odd-point model (proved): on a knot space with a line M removed, choosing each line's odd point (the one whose signed value differs from the other two) is a bijection between the solutions up to complement and the choices of one incidence per line whose number on every cycle of the incidence graph without M has the parity of that cycle's signs; checked at all 56 census removals. (2) The skip model (proved): on a plane knot space whose signs satisfy Kasteleyn's face condition (a face of length 2k has k + 1 negative incidences mod 2), call the corner of a line opposite its odd point the corner it skips; the cycle conditions say that every face holds an odd number of skipped corners. Euler's formula gives n + 2 faces for n lines, so the knot fails by counting. After a line M is removed (its three corners count as skipped), every face holds exactly one skipped corner, so the solutions up to complement are exactly the perfect matchings of the other lines to the faces off M, each line to one of its own faces. Checked on 17 plane knot spaces at every removal; every failing signing of the planar census spaces (488) satisfies the face condition. (3) Interfaces (proved): a line's possible odd points are the incidences opposite its faces matched to it in some such matching, so a line meeting M shares a face with M and has at most four port patterns (checked on 1494 pairs). (4) Handles (proved count, computed example): on a surface of genus g there are n + 2 - 2g faces and 2g further cycle parities, so counting no longer forces failure. On the Fano plane's 16 torus embeddings (7 hexagons) the knot's signs satisfy the face condition, and after a removal 14 face-odd skip assignments remain, each with one face skipped three times, of which the two homology parities keep 5. (5) Open: that a planar removed side never creates (ticket A, finite); the skip model reduces it to perfect matchings of lines to faces in which the closing line's matched face carries the interface.
failure_conditions: A plane knot space with face-condition signs on which the knot does not fail.
A removal from such a space whose solutions up to complement are not the perfect matchings of the other lines to the faces off the removed line.
A line meeting the removed line in a point with six port patterns, on a plane knot space.
A torus embedding of the Fano plane on which the knot's signs violate the face condition.
foundation_claim_scope: Knot spaces whose incidence graph is embedded on an orientable surface, with signs satisfying the face condition.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-02.
validation.status: proved (odd-point model, skip model, interfaces, counting) and checked on the census, 17 plane knot spaces and the Fano plane's torus embeddings; the planar non-creation statement remains a conjecture; no human or external review
validation.novelty: The skip model and its corollaries are new here as stated; Kasteleyn's face condition and Moret's planar not-all-equal results are classical.
